---
title: "Mental Health in Tech: Policy Report in R Markdown"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "/kaggle/input/mental-health-in-tech-survey-5k/mental_health_tech.csv",
  "/kaggle/input/datasets/lorenzoscaturchio/mental-health-in-tech-survey-5k/mental_health_tech.csv",
  "mental_health_tech.csv"
)

data_path <- NA_character_
for (candidate in candidate_paths) {
  if (file.exists(candidate)) {
    data_path <- candidate
    break
  }
}

if (is.na(data_path) && dir.exists("/kaggle/input")) {
  matches <- list.files(
    "/kaggle/input",
    pattern = "^mental_health_tech\\.csv$",
    recursive = TRUE,
    full.names = TRUE
  )
  if (length(matches) > 0) {
    data_path <- matches[[1]]
  }
}

if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("mental_health_tech.csv not found in /kaggle/input or local working directory")
}

survey <- read.csv(data_path)
```

# Overview

This report evaluates which employer support signals are most associated with workers seeking treatment, using the Mental Health in Tech dataset.

```{r}
survey %>%
  group_by(benefits, seek_help) %>%
  summarise(
    respondents = n(),
    treatment_rate = mean(treatment == "Yes"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

# Treatment rate by support environment

```{r}
ggplot(
  survey,
  aes(x = reorder(benefits, as.numeric(treatment == "Yes"), FUN = mean), y = as.numeric(treatment == "Yes"))
) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "col") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Treatment rate by employer mental health benefits",
    x = "Benefits response",
    y = "Share seeking treatment"
  )
```

# Country and company-size slice

```{r}
survey %>%
  group_by(country, no_employees) %>%
  summarise(
    respondents = n(),
    treatment_rate = mean(treatment == "Yes"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(respondents)) %>%
  head(20)
```
